title: Wardith prospect-compiler campaign input
description: A validated, structured market-run dataset, prepared by Claude/human judgement during a Wardith sector x local-market campaign. build_workbook.py renders this deterministically into an .xlsx workbook. It does not do research or judgement. Version 2 (2026-08-16) generalizes the auditable v2.1 scoring methodology (see CAMPAIGN-HANDOFF.md Section 3a) into the canonical schema: service-scope classification, question-relevance classification, a documented 14-field scoring model, structured decision-maker accessibility, and overall/outreach ranking. All v2 fields are additive and optional so pre-v2 campaign JSON files remain valid historical records; a campaign qualified going forward is expected to populate them.

question_entry.description: One campaign question. question_id matches the question_id used in the raw trade-run CSV and mention-counts.json (e.g. 'q01') - the join key between a question's text and its relevance classification and per-question appearance counts.

service_scope_def.description: One campaign-defined service-scope label (e.g. 'kitchen_only', 'bathroom_only', 'combined' for a kitchen-and-bathroom campaign; a different vocabulary entirely for a different sector). applicable_services names which of the campaign's real-world services this scope genuinely offers - this is what question-relevance weighting keys off, not the label string itself.

scoring_cohort_entry.description: One business explicitly placed in the canonical scoring cohort for this campaign, per CAMPAIGN-HANDOFF.md Section 3a's candidate-pool-consistency rule. Every business meeting run.cohort_inclusion_min_appearances must have an entry here with a real status - the mechanism that stops a high-appearance business (e.g. one found late, or one that looked hard to research) from silently staying an unscored market[] record while lower-appearance businesses got the full scoring pass.

status.description: SCORED: this business has service_scope set and appears in the scored pool (market[]/outreach[]). EXCLUDED: a documented reason (see 'reason') ruled it out of scoring, distinct from schema-level excluded_entry.reason though it may reuse the same value. INCOMPLETE: research is not yet sufficient to score or exclude it - see 'missing_evidence'.

reason.description: Required when status is EXCLUDED - why this cohort member was not scored.

missing_evidence.description: Required when status is INCOMPLETE - exactly what evidence is still needed.

question_relevance_entry.description: The relevance classification of one campaign question, per CAMPAIGN-HANDOFF.md Section 3a. SERVICE_ONLY requires 'service' (must match a value that appears in at least one service_scope_def's applicable_services). AMBIGUOUS requires 'weight' (0 excludes the question from relevant-question scoring entirely; a fraction applies a documented partial weight; the field must not be silently omitted, defaulting a question to full relevance by accident).

scoring_fields.description: The auditable v2.1 scoring model, generalized. Every 0-5 field's scale, every formula, every threshold, and every gate is documented in CAMPAIGN-HANDOFF.md Section 3a - this schema only enforces shape and range, not the reasoning behind a value. VALUE fields (commercial_fit, service_relevance, business_credibility, ability_to_buy, decision_maker_identified, direct_dm_route, contact_route_quality, contact_identity_confidence, research_completeness, active_entity_verified, live_website_verified, contact_route_exists) are Claude's evidence-backed judgement calls - the last three are not currently consumed by scoring_engine.py (formerly GAP's lighter gate, retired 2026-08-24). DERIVED fields (visibility_rate, visibility_score, relative_position, question_coverage, gap_strength, overall_evidence_confidence, final_score, overall_rank, outreach_rank, most_named_cohort, and the *_verified/*_complete/eligible_for_outreach gates) must be produced by tools/prospect-compiler/scoring_engine.py, never hand-computed or hand-typed - see CAMPAIGN-HANDOFF.md Section 3a's 'formulas, not vibes' rule.

narrative_generated_from.description: AUTO, written by scoring_engine.py only, for a scored (service_scope set) entry: a fingerprint of the structured values competitive_gap_finding/why_prospect were generated from. Recomputed and compared on every scoring_engine.py run - a mismatch forces regeneration, so a re-score can never leave a stale narrative behind merely because the field was already non-empty. Absent entirely means the narrative has never been machine-generated/verified against current values - build_workbook.py --require-scored rejects this for a new campaign; the default (non-strict) render flags it as a QC warning instead. Never hand-set.

fact_category.description: Optional grouping so evidence for different kinds of claims about the same business can be told apart at a glance - see CAMPAIGN-HANDOFF.md Section 3a's evidence-separation rule.

questions.description: As of schema v2, an array of {question_id, text} objects (was an array of plain strings pre-v2) so question_relevance[] and every business's question_appearances can key off a stable, short ID instead of repeating full question text.

responses_per_question.description: AUTO: runs x providers for a single question, e.g. 5 runs x 3 providers = 15. Assumes every question in this campaign was run the same number of times across the same providers (true for every trade_run.py campaign to date) - the weighted-denominator formula in scoring_engine.py depends on this being uniform; a campaign that genuinely varies run-count per question is a documented limitation, not yet supported.

cohort_inclusion_min_appearances.description: The mechanical floor of this campaign's stated candidate-pool inclusion threshold (CAMPAIGN-HANDOFF.md Section 3a): any market[]/outreach[] business with total_ai_appearances at or above this number must have a matching entry in run.scoring_cohort. A business below the floor may still be included in the cohort by judgement: this is a floor, not the whole rule - the qualitative parts of the inclusion rule stay in methodology_notes. Required, and mechanically enforced, only when build_workbook.py is run with --require-scored.

gap_cohort_min_appearances.description: 2026-08-23. A second, lighter, separately-capped floor for GAP eligibility specifically - may be 0, since a zero-appearance business is the strongest GAP case there is. Governs the lighter research pass (active_entity_verified/live_website_verified/contact_route_exists) for a business below cohort_inclusion_min_appearances. Required, and mechanically cross-checked against gap_cohort_cap and the scored pool, only when build_workbook.py is run with --require-scored; historical campaigns without it remain readable.

gap_cohort_cap.description: 2026-08-23. The maximum number of below-cohort_inclusion_min_appearances businesses researched via the lighter GAP gate in this run - stated as data before researching anyone, same discipline as cohort_inclusion_min_appearances, chosen per campaign from real cost evidence rather than invented in advance. A below-floor business beyond this cap stays INCOMPLETE in run.scoring_cohort, not silently dropped.

scoring_cohort.description: The complete, explicit candidate cohort selected for canonical qualification this campaign - every business is SCORED, EXCLUDED (with a reason), or INCOMPLETE (with the missing evidence stated), so none can silently disappear into an unscored market[] record. Required, and mechanically cross-checked against cohort_inclusion_min_appearances and the scored pool, only when build_workbook.py is run with --require-scored; historical campaigns without it remain readable.

service_scopes.description: Every service-scope label used anywhere in this campaign's market[]/outreach[] entries, defined once here per CAMPAIGN-HANDOFF.md Section 3a.

question_relevance.description: The relevance classification of every question in 'questions' above, per CAMPAIGN-HANDOFF.md Section 3a. Required for a v2 campaign wherever service_scope/visibility_score fields are populated on any business - scoring_engine.py refuses to compute relevance-normalized visibility without it.
